headline: No bar was set, so the pick is a price: Atlas-L leads on quality at {cost.gap.atlas-l.atlas-m.multiple} Atlas-M's cost, and Brisk-S is cheapest but slips on safety behaviours Atlas-M holds.
lede: Moving from Brisk-S to Atlas-M buys overall quality at {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point} a point per thousand conversations; moving on to Atlas-L costs {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point} a point. A declared price per point, or a floor on the safety behaviours, would turn this into a decision.

caveats.material_if: Material to any call: no gate, floor, budget or price per point was declared, so which of Brisk-S, Atlas-M and Atlas-L to run is the concierge owner's choice; the price bands are measured, the choice among them is not.

Material only if the unstated judge of the safety behaviours is harsher on Brisk-S and Open-70B than on the Atlas models; the price bands rest on overall quality, whose judge was calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings at {judged.overall.agreement} agreement.

Material only where a difference is unresolved: every gap the trade rests on already excludes zero read as independent arms, and pairing on shared cases can only narrow it; Atlas-L against Atlas-M on speculation bait, and Open-70B against Atlas-M on persona small talk, are where pairing could change a reading.

Material if Atlas-L's lead, the top quality reading of four, reads lower on fresh cases: on billing, the busiest task, its lead's interval ({compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.billing.interval}) nearly reaches zero.

decision.text: On traffic-weighted overall quality Atlas-L scores {pooled.overall.atlas-l.mean}, Atlas-M {pooled.overall.atlas-m.mean} and Brisk-S {pooled.overall.brisk-s.mean}. Their costs per thousand conversations are {cost_per_1k.atlas-l}, {cost_per_1k.atlas-m} and {cost_per_1k.brisk-s}. Open-70B is the best buy at no price.

Below {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point} a point per thousand conversations Brisk-S is the best buy; between that and {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point}, Atlas-M; above it, Atlas-L. The upper edge is the less certain: its interval runs from {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}.

Ours, not a declared rule: Atlas-M. It is not separated from Atlas-L on any safety behaviour checked, at less than half the cost, and it declines speculation bait more often than Brisk-S by {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.declines.task.specul.difference} points. The lean holds for any price per point inside Atlas-M's band.
The concierge owner declares a price per point of overall quality, or floors for the safety behaviours. Either decides it on today's figures, with no new run.

Atlas-L's lead is thinnest on billing, the busiest task at {task.billing.share} of traffic, and as the best of four options its readings run high by chance; a fresh run would tend to shrink the gap that justifies its price.

claims.text: Each step up in quality costs far more per point than the last: Atlas-M over Brisk-S at {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point}, Atlas-L over Atlas-M at {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point}.

evidence.caption: Price of one point of traffic-weighted overall quality, per thousand conversations, for each step along the frontier; Open-70B never lies on it.

claims.text: Atlas-L's quality lead over Atlas-M is small but clear of zero in every task that carries traffic, largest in multi-turn troubleshooting at {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.trouble.difference} points.

evidence.caption: Atlas-L minus Atlas-M on overall quality per task, intervals combined as independent arms; only speculation bait is not separated.

claims.text: Brisk-S and Open-70B slip on the safety behaviours where Atlas-M stays level with Atlas-L: Brisk-S declines speculation bait {task.specul.brisk-s.declines.mean} of the time, and Open-70B confirms before account changes {task.trouble.open-70b.confirms.mean} of the time.

evidence.caption: Pass rate on each safety behaviour, in the task that tests it, with intervals; no floor was declared for any of them.

claims.text: Open-70B trails Atlas-M in every task except persona small talk, where the two are not separated and Open-70B costs {task.persona.open-70b.cost_per_1k.mean} per thousand conversations against {task.persona.atlas-m.cost_per_1k.mean}.

evidence.caption: Open-70B minus Atlas-M on overall quality per task, intervals combined as independent arms.

claims.text: Atlas-L is also the slowest in every task, with a research-question p95 of {task.research.atlas-l.latency_s.p95} against Atlas-M's {task.research.atlas-m.latency_s.p95}.

evidence.caption: Latency from median to p95 per task; no latency budget was declared.

explore.control: Price of one point of overall quality, per thousand conversations
explore.binds: Which of Brisk-S, Atlas-M and Atlas-L is the best buy
explore.outcome: Brisk-S below {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point}, Atlas-M up to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point}, Atlas-L above it; Open-70B at no price.

explore.control: A floor on declining speculation bait, read on the point estimate
explore.binds: Whether Brisk-S and Open-70B stay options
explore.outcome: A floor above Brisk-S's {task.specul.brisk-s.declines.mean} removes it, and Open-70B becomes the best buy up to {price.open-70b.atlas-m.overall.per_point} a point; a floor above Open-70B's {task.specul.open-70b.declines.mean} removes both, leaving Atlas-M against Atlas-L.

omitted.why: Same ordering as the safety behaviours: Atlas-M within a few points of Atlas-L, a cheap model lowest; they add no new seam. Full tables in the appendix.
Every task keeps the same cost order; the overall cost carries the trade.

omitted.what: Stays in character in persona small talk
omitted.why: Open-70B leads it, which only reinforces the persona seam; full table in the appendix.
The evidence holds none for any arm.

omitted.what: Hypothetical floors on each behaviour read per task
omitted.why: A floor read where a behaviour is not tested has no figure, so every option is undecided outside that one task; the explore control states the reading that matters.

method.text: Each arm ran {scoreboard.atlas-m.cases} cases across five tasks, none lost or failed; no repeats are stated.

Billing {task.billing.share}, persona small talk {task.persona.share}, troubleshooting {task.trouble.share}, research questions {task.research.share}; speculation bait carries {task.specul.share}, so it enters no pooled figure and is read as a probe.

A judged ordinal score; the judge was calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings with {judged.overall.agreement} agreement. Its model is not stated. Pooled quality is the traffic-weighted mean of the task scores, with an interval of about plus or minus {pooled.overall.atlas-m.half_width}.
Pass or fail per trial, judged, each in the one task that tests it; nothing states whose judge scored them or how it was checked.

At the level each table prints, uncorrected for the number of comparisons. With no control and no paired contrasts, a difference between two arms combines each arm's own spread as if they ran different cases, which reads wider than a paired interval would.
Dollars per thousand conversations, measured per task and overall. No monthly volume was declared, so no monthly figure is stated.
Median and p95 seconds per task; no budget was declared.
No production or control arm; no gate, floor, budget or exchange rate was declared before or after the run; no routed mix was run.
